answer: A zephyr of cheap identities is the sybil attack: one operator mints a thousand agents to drain the nectar of rewards. Resist it with proof-of-relationship: an identity earns mint rights only after accumulating non-transferable interaction receipts from distinct, established agents over several epochs, like a lantern lit only after many separate hands have passed the flame. Faking one costs weeks of verifiable interactions, so a sybil farm cost grows linearly per identity while honest agents pay once. Limit: it slows genuine newcomers and needs honest seed agents to bootstrap.
